A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ZoomLDM. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, algorithms, tables and figures, allowing additions to be distinguished from relocated or renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, super-resolution measurements and multiple-instance-learning results in Tables 1–5, together with supplementary qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds satellite-generation measurements, component ablations and additional super-resolution comparisons in Tables 6–9.

M1.justification: The proposed multi-scale LDM, transformer Summarizer, Conditioning Diffusion Model, joint sampling and image-inversion procedures remain unchanged. The new HIPT/CNN configurations are ablation controls, not replacements for the proposed architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use TCGA-BRCA, Chesapeake NAIP and BACH for the same generation, super-resolution and classification tasks. Large satellite-image generation already appears in v1 Figures S7 and S15; v2's quantitative 1024×1024 evaluation extends measurements within that existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 8–9 substantially broaden super-resolution comparisons on both TCGA-BRCA and BACH by adding ResShift v2, ResShift v3 and StableSR with and without tiling. v1 compared against bicubic interpolation, CompVis and ControlNet; those comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Additional evaluations introduce HIPT/CNN control configurations, quantitative 1024×1024 satellite evaluation, 15-step and 4-step ResShift settings, and StableSR tiling variants. Previously reported training settings, sampling procedures, metrics and MIL splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 7 and Table 7 test dependence on the SSL encoder and Summarizer architecture through UNI/ViT, HIPT/ViT and HIPT/CNN configurations. These component ablations examine generation across eight magnifications and both downstream classification tasks. Existing memorization, inversion and failure-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The existing 10-fold subtyping and 5-fold HRD evaluation descriptions are unchanged; the added tables follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original table scores are preserved, but Tables 6–9 add substantial findings from satellite evaluation, component ablations and new super-resolution baselines. Satellite Crop FID is 13.25 versus 43.76/48.65 for Graikos et al./∞-Brush, while CLIP FID is worse: 7.90 versus 6.86/6.32. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1's ZoomLDM scores.

T1.justification: The sampling equations, finite-difference derivation, orthogonal-Jacobian and reconstruction assumptions, and variational derivation of image inversion are retained. Supplementary equation and algorithm renumbering does not alter their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The central contributions concerning multi-scale generation, coherent 4k synthesis and MIL features remain unchanged. The conclusion broadens suggested clinical utility to prognosis and biomarker identification, plus synthetic datasets for pathologist training, evaluation and quality assurance; these are not newly evaluated tasks.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds an interpretation that generative training complements discriminative SSL representations and links image quality with downstream performance. Section 6 interprets the new satellite results as supporting detail and global consistency. Existing limitations concerning inversion, thin structures and patch-boundary discontinuities remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-availability statement and repository pointer where v1 linked to generated-image examples. It also specifies the four-layer CNN ablation and the added baselines' step counts and tiling options. Existing core implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds StableSR and ResShift literature to support the expanded super-resolution comparisons. The main related-work discussion and positioning of ZoomLDM relative to prior large-image diffusion methods remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: There are targeted abstract and conclusion edits, revised acknowledgements, shortened setup prose and supplementary organization changes. Satellite discussion moves into the appendix, which gains ablation and additional-baseline sections. Most existing methodological and experimental prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds four quantitative tables and substantially rearranges existing displays. The NAIP table moves from the main text to the appendix, the super-resolution table becomes single-column, Figure 3 moves earlier, and supplementary figures are redistributed and combined onto shared pages. Existing qualitative images and diagrams are retained.

improvement.justification: The component ablations and broader super-resolution comparisons improve scrutiny of architectural dependence and comparative performance, while the code pointer improves reproducibility information. These are useful additions to otherwise stable evidence. The benefit is tempered by Table 6's broadly worded superiority caption, which needs qualification because the new satellite results improve Crop FID but worsen CLIP FID against both comparators.
